findings.evidence: A `required: true` doc-type absent at or before the current stage → note it to the user as a prerequisite to produce next
findings.fix: Name the field and the file: a doc_types entry whose frontmatter sets required: true in the resolved FRAMEWORK_PROFILE_PATH, and say the Surface message lists it as a prerequisite gap rather than a finding.

findings.evidence: Use when a design, spec, requirements, or plan document needs review-and-fix before the next step.
findings.fix: Review a design, spec, requirements or plan and, when the user authorizes revisions, loop a clean-context reviewer with the matching fixer until approved or the iteration cap. Use when asked to review or review-and-fix a spec, plan, design, requirements or RFC before the next step, even if they only say 'review this doc' or pass a path, including --cross-ai and --no-cross-ai. Keywords: superpowers, GSD, OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Kiro, BMAD, PLAN.md, docs/superpowers, .planning, openspec. Not for writing a new spec or plan, executing a plan, reviewing a pull-request diff, or configuring cross-AI reviewers (ai-kit-spec-config).

findings.evidence: MANDATORY — READ ENTIRE FILE, on every run: Before running any command below, read references/cross-ai-dispatch.md completely
findings.fix: Keep the every-run read for points 0-2 (paths, RUN_TMP_DIR, session-default list). Gate the rest: read the probe, trust and ladder sections only when --cross-ai is on; read the pending-lane and Step 1 subprocess sections only on exit 69 or 75.

findings.evidence: 20 queries, 10 should-trigger and 10 should-not-trigger, but no casual or typo phrasings among the positives
findings.fix: Add two should-trigger queries a user would actually type without naming the skill or a framework, for example a terse 'look over this plan and fix it' and one with a typo, and keep the near-miss negatives.

findings.evidence: ## NEVER (hard landmines) lists two items, then defers the rest to ## Hard rules for the orchestrator
findings.fix: Add a short Gotchas list in SKILL.md for the three failures the steps already name: grounding against the wrong worktree, reviewing an intent doc with a plan checklist, and re-dispatching a failed subprocess lane to another model.

findings.evidence: Process pattern is right, but the body is an operator runbook of verbatim commands rather than a thinking framework that generalises
findings.fix: Keep the commands in the references. Open each step with the one question the orchestrator must answer (already done at 0.5, 0.7, 3 and 5) and leave the snippets to the mandatory reads.

findings.evidence: Dispatch for both: fresh-context delegation (Step 1) — on Claude Code the Agent tool with subagent_type: general-purpose.
findings.fix: Move the Claude Code Agent-tool restatement to references/cli-profiles/claude.md; keep only the non-obvious rule that a host with no clean-context tool must not review inline.

findings.evidence: Without Node, the probe walk marks subprocess entries unavailable before dispatch ... a dispatch that hits it is a dispatch_unavailable Failure, never a session-default run.
findings.fix: Keep the fail-closed rule. State the one default the owner can take when Node is absent: re-invoke with --no-cross-ai so only the native session reviewer runs.
